q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Net sales did not drop yesterday — they more than doubled: order-date net sales were ₹91,220 on 2026-10-13 vs ₹42,177 on 2026-10-12 (+116%). (Measured)

Evidence (2026-10-12 → 2026-10-13)
- Measured — Net sales: ₹42,177 → ₹91,220 (+116%)
- Measured — Orders: 26 → 45 (+73%)
- Measured — Net AOV: ₹2,116 → ₹2,694 (+27%)
- Measured — Conversion rate: 0.5% → 1.1%
- Measured — Ad spend (P&L basis): ₹38,661 → ₹50,426 (+30%)
- Measured — Refunded amount (ex-GST): ₹2,598 → ₹61,122 (large spike)

Interpretation (short)
- Diagnose found no single supported cause; the day’s increase is within the metric’s normal variation. (Measured)
- The refund amount did spike sharply but the causal test ruled it out as a driver of the sales change. (Measured → ruled out)
- Ad spend, sessions and conversions moved together with sales — they correlate but the analysis could not establish a directional cause. (Hypothesis: correlated, not proven)

Basis: order-date figures for default brand (Tilting Heads).
